title: Exam Oracle sealed prediction
description: Written by B's rank_and_seal.py, rendered by C's dashboard and reveal. The SHA-256 seal is computed over the canonical JSON of THIS object (json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8')). The hash is stored next to the file (<run_id>.sha256) and in the ledger, never inside the object.

lessons_run_seq.description: Lessons version used; null = cold-start weights

standardization.description: How the signals enter p. zscore_per_run_v1 (D5): each of x1..x7 is z-scored across THIS prediction's topics (population std; a signal with zero variance gives 0 for every topic), then p = sigma(intercept + sum_k w_k * z_k). The topics' `signals` keep the RAW x values. Absent: p = sigma(intercept + sum_k w_k * x_k) on the raw values.

weights.description: The beta weights used for this prediction (the lessons)

topics.description: Every predictable topic of the course's fixed list, sorted by rank ascending. The off-list bucket T00 is never listed (D6): it is never ranked or predicted, but answer-key points on it stay in the scoring denominator

even.description: topic_ids chosen by baseline A (study evenly); empty when lecture data is not visible (exam_history runs use the closed-form expectation k/N at scoring)

last_exam.description: topic_ids chosen by baseline B (copy last exam)
